ach.barbershop_10: Change looks 10 times in the barbershop
ach.collect_theme_all_parts_1: Collect all parts of a theme
ach.craft_outfit_weapon_theme: Craft an outfit, a weapon and a theme
ach.stimpacks_100_radaway_100: Use 100 stimpaks and 100 RadAway on quests
act.resetAll: File restored to its original state
aerr.edit: The change could not be applied: {detail}
aerr.incidentActive: An incident is already in progress. End it first.
aerr.notAllowed: This value is not allowed in normal mode.
aerr.notInCatalog: This id is not in the reference data. Use expert mode to enter any id.
aerr.outOfRange: Allowed range: {min}–{max}. Enable expert mode to enter other values.
aerr.outfitGender: The game has no version of this outfit for this dweller's gender. On load it would put a random casual outfit on instead.
aerr.roomBusy: The room has dead dwellers, a couple, children or an item being crafted. Finish that first or use expert mode.
aerr.roomDisconnected: The room would not be connected to the vault door, or other rooms would lose their connection.
aerr.roomFixed: The vault door and the wasteland exit cannot be changed.
aerr.roomLocked: The room is not unlocked in the blueprint book (or is built and cannot be locked): the game would crash on load.
aerr.roomOverlap: The room would overlap a neighbouring room or rocks, or leave the vault grid.
aerr.roomSize: The game has no room of this type with this size or upgrade level: the save would not load.
aerr.roomUnique: The game allows only one room of this type.
aerr.tooManyDwellers: A vault holds at most 200 dwellers.
aerr.wrongType: This field has a different type.
app.name: ShelterSave-Studio
app.unaffiliated: Independent project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Bethesda Softworks or ZeniMax Media.
art.mismatch: The installed game version differs from the editor's catalog, so the picture is not available.
art.noGame: Pictures come from the installed game. The game was not found: set its folder in the settings.
art.web.badFile: This is not the game file {name}. Choose FalloutShelter_Data\{name} from the game folder.
art.web.desktopNote: The desktop version finds the installed game by itself, no file needs to be chosen.
art.web.file: The file data.unity3d (about 460 MB) from the FalloutShelter_Data folder of the PC version of the game: Steam or Bethesda.net. Pictures and the phrases of the wasteland journal are read from it.
art.web.loadHelp: Choose FalloutShelter_Data\data.unity3d from the folder of the game installed on this PC. The file is read only in this tab.
art.web.loading: Reading pictures from the game file… {pct}%
art.web.noTexts: The phrases of the wasteland journal are not shown on the website, only the values.
art.web.none: Game pictures are not shown on the website.
art.web.paste: Tip: copy the path, paste it into the File name field of the file window and press Enter.
art.web.phone: Android and other phone versions keep this data inside the app, so the file cannot be chosen there. Open the site on a computer with the game installed.
art.web.private: The file is read only in this tab: it is not uploaded or saved anywhere. After closing or reloading the tab the pictures are gone and the file has to be chosen again.
art.web.ready: Pictures are loaded from your game file for this tab.
art.web.steam: In the Steam library, right-click Fallout Shelter and choose Manage → Browse local files. Open the FalloutShelter_Data folder: data.unity3d is there.
art.web.steamOther: If the game is in another Steam library, the path starts with that library, for example D:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Fallout Shelter\FalloutShelter_Data.
art.web.title: Game pictures
art.web.version: The pictures match game version {v}. After a game update some pictures may be missing until the site is updated.
art.web.why: The website does not store or send any images of the game: they belong to the game's rights holders. You can still see them: your browser can read them from your own copy of the game on this device.
c.dangerDelete: Delete {n} dwellers? References to them are removed everywhere in the file. You can undo this.
c.fieldUnknown: A technical field of the game. Its effect is not described; change it only if you know what it does.
c.noResults: Nothing found. Try another word or clear the filters.
close.text: There are unsaved changes. Close without saving?
close.title: Unsaved changes
dw.cloneHelp: Adds a copy of this dweller with the same stats, looks and equipment.
dw.colorPick: Click to open or close the palette
dw.emptyVault: There are no dwellers in this vault yet.
dw.faceMaskHelp: What the dweller wears on the face. Beards are offered to men only, as in the game; glasses, make-up and masks to everyone.
dw.fromJournalHelp: Add a legendary dweller the way the game gives one: name, looks, SPECIAL, outfit, weapon and journal entry.
dw.gameColor: One of the colours the game itself gives dwellers
dw.hairStyleHelp: Every hairstyle the game has for this gender. "Special" ones belong to legendary dwellers.
dw.handyAdd: Give a Mr. Handy (in a box)
dw.handyAddHelp: Adds a Mr. Handy box to the lunchboxes, the way the game gives robots. In the game open it and place the robot on a floor.
dw.handyCollectHelp: Ticked when the robot collects ready resources on its floor by itself.
dw.handyHealthHelp: The game caps it at the robot's full health.
dw.helmetHelp: A hat from the barber shop. The game wears either a hat or a beard/glasses/mask, so choosing one removes the other. An outfit's own helmet is shown instead; some hats are taken off inside the vault and are seen only in the wasteland.
dw.importBad: This file could not be read as a Fallout Shelter save.
dw.importEmpty: There are no dwellers in that save.
dw.importHelp: Copy dwellers from another save file into this vault. The other file is only read.
dw.importNote: They arrive with their level, SPECIAL, look, outfit, weapon and pet, but without a room, partner or family from the other vault. Items this game does not know are replaced with the jumpsuit and fists.
dw.journalHelp: The game adds such a dweller or pet together with a journal entry (marked new). The dweller's outfit and weapon also appear in the journal. The dweller arrives at level 1.
dw.levelHelp: 1–50. Experience and maximum health change the way the game does it.
dw.mass.fieldHelp: Sets the same value of the chosen field for every selected dweller.
dw.massHint: Tick several dwellers in the list to change them all at once.
dw.none: Select a dweller in the list.
dw.outfitColorFixed: This outfit has one colour in the game, it does not change.
dw.outfitColorHelp: Each outfit has its own set of colours. On load the game replaces any other colour with the nearest one from the set, so only these can be chosen.
dw.outfitColorPregnant: While pregnant the dweller wears the maternity dress; its colour does not change.
dw.outfitColorWrong: The outfit has no version for this gender, so the game picks a random casual outfit and its colour itself.
dw.petFromJournalHelp: Add a legendary pet to storage with its journal entry.
dw.petsHelp: Pets and Mr. Handy robots living in the vault. A pet is given to a dweller in the Equipment block of that dweller.
dw.previewHelp: How the game draws this dweller inside the vault: skin, hairstyle and hair colour, beard or mask, face by mood, and the outfit worn with its colour. Helmets the game takes off in the vault are not shown; weapon and pet are not shown.
dw.previewLoading: Loading the picture from the game files…
dw.previewNoHeadgear: The big headgear of this outfit is drawn by the game separately and is not shown here.
dw.previewNoOutfit: This outfit is not in the game files found here, so the basic jumpsuit is shown.
dw.previewWrongGender: This outfit has no version for this gender. In the game the dweller will wear a random casual outfit instead, so the basic jumpsuit is shown.
dw.sort.name: Name
dw.specialHelp.1: Strength: work speed in power rooms (Power Generator, Nuclear Reactor). Trained in the Weight Room.
dw.specialHelp.2: Perception: work speed in water rooms. Trained in the Armory.
dw.specialHelp.3: Endurance: health gained with each level and resistance in the wasteland. Raise it before levelling up. Trained in the Fitness Room.
dw.specialHelp.4: Charisma: work in the Radio Studio and Living Quarters, faster relationships. Trained in the Lounge.
dw.specialHelp.5: Intelligence: work speed in the Medbay and Science Lab. Trained in the Classroom.
dw.specialHelp.6: Agility: work speed in food rooms and the Nuka-Cola Bottler, attack speed in fights. Trained in the Athletics Room.
dw.specialHelp.7: Luck: more caps and items, better chance of a successful rush. Trained in the Game Room.
dw.waitingHelp: Dwellers who came to the vault and wait for you to let them in. They are already in the dweller list.
dw.wlTimeHelp: Time on the current trip. Objectives like "explore the wasteland for N hours" count it.
err.bad_length: The file is cut off or damaged: its length is wrong for an encrypted save.
err.bad_padding: The file could not be decrypted. It is damaged or encrypted with another key.
err.io: The file could not be read or written: {detail}
err.not_base64: This is not a Fallout Shelter save: its text is not Base64. Check that you chose a .sav file.
err.not_json: The data inside is not valid JSON ({detail}). The file is damaged.
err.not_object: The data has an unexpected structure: a vault object was expected.
err.not_utf8: The decrypted data is not text. The file is damaged.
err.title: The file could not be opened
err.too_large: The file is larger than 32 MB. Saves are much smaller; this is probably a different file.
err.what: What to do: open a backup copy or another save.
first.text: Read the license and the privacy policy. The program does not collect or send any data.

integ.actor_counter: Pet id counter {value} is not above the largest id {max}
integ.actor_id_duplicate: Pet actor id {id} is used twice
integ.color_alpha: A color of dweller {id} is not fully opaque
integ.dweller_in_two_rooms: Dweller {id} is listed in rooms {other} and {room}
integ.happiness_list_mismatch: Happiness records and their list disagree (id {id})
integ.happiness_stale: Happiness record {key} belongs to a missing room or dweller
integ.lunchbox_count: Box counter {value} differs from the number of boxes {expected}
integ.manual: Needs manual repair in expert mode
integ.partner_not_mutual: Dweller {id} has partner {partner}, but not the other way round
integ.pet_owner_missing: A pet follows dweller {id}, who does not exist
integ.quest_dweller_missing: The quest team refers to missing dweller {id}
integ.requirement_dweller_missing: An objective refers to missing dweller {id}
integ.room_counter: Room id counter {value} is below the largest id {max}
integ.room_dweller_missing: Room {room} lists dweller {id}, who does not exist
integ.room_locked: Room "{room}" is built but not unlocked in the blueprint book: the game will crash on load
integ.room_shape: Room "{room}" has size {merge} and level {level}, which the game does not have: the game hangs while loading
integ.saved_room_missing: A dweller refers to missing room {room}

journal.resetHelp: Removes all edits. This step can be undone too.
journal.title: History of changes
map.copyNoSpot: There is no free place for a room of this size that connects to the vault. Click the map to choose a place.
map.disconnected: The room would not be connected to the vault door through rooms and elevators.
map.disconnectedExpert: Not connected to the vault door: dwellers cannot walk there and the game may behave oddly.
map.dragHint: Drag to move, click to change.
map.fixed: This room cannot be moved or removed.
map.keysHelp: Keyboard: select a room, move it with Alt and the arrow keys, press Enter to place it or Escape to cancel.
map.locked: "{room}" is not unlocked in the blueprint book yet. If it is built without unlocking, the game crashes when the save loads.
map.lockedShort: not unlocked in the blueprint book
map.outOfGrid: The room does not fit into the vault here.
map.overlap: The room would overlap another room or rocks.
map.placeRockHelp: Puts rocks on two free cells, as on a new floor in the game.
map.rockHelp: Rocks block two cells: nothing can be built there. In the game they are cleared for caps.
map.rockHint: Rocks. Click to select and remove.
map.sizeHelp: How many rooms are merged: 1, 2 or 3. Each step adds 3 cells and 2 places for dwellers.
map.typeHelp: Rooms that the game lets you build. The vault door, the wasteland exit and the ultracite mine are not listed.
map.unique: This room is already built. The game allows only one.
map.unlockBuildHelp: Marks the room unlocked in the blueprint book (as if you opened it in the game) and builds it. It is one step: Undo reverts both.
o.achievementToggleHelp: Tick to give the achievement, untick to take it back in the save.
o.achievementsHelp: Achievements earned in this vault. A ticked achievement is sent to Steam when the game loads the save. Unticking takes it back only in the save: Steam keeps an achievement once it is unlocked. Untick an achievement to make the game count its progress again from the start.
o.bottleChanceHelp: Added to the base chance at the next check. 100% means they come at the next check. The game resets it to 0 after a visit.
o.bottleHelp: The Nuka-Cola mascots sometimes walk through the vault and make dwellers happier. The game checks from time to time whether they come; each failed check raises the chance.
o.bottleLockedHelp: Ticked after a visit: the game waits before the next one. Untick so they can come again.
o.bottleUnlockInHelp: While locked, Bottle and Cappy do not appear; the lock ends when this timer runs out.
o.capsFoundHelp: Caps the explorer carries. They go to the vault storage when the dweller comes back.
o.collectedResHelp: Totals from the statistics window. Changing them does not give resources: the vault storage is on the Vault page.
o.completeObjectiveHelp: Marks the objective as done, as if its goal was reached. In the game, open the objectives list and collect the reward; the game then gives a new objective.
o.completeTutorial: Finish the tutorial and turn off hints
o.completeTutorialHelp: Marks every tutorial step and hint as already shown, so the game stops showing them.
o.completedQuestsHelp: Ticked quests count as completed: the game opens the next quests of their storylines and does not offer them again. Untick a quest to play it again.
o.currentObjectivesHelp: The three objectives shown in the game. A completed objective gives its reward when you collect it in the game. Any objective can be replaced with another one, and its difficulty can be changed: the goal and the reward grow with it.
o.dailyWeeklyHelp: Quests the game offers now. Any of them can be replaced with another quest of the same kind. If the game cannot offer the chosen quest yet, it picks another one when the save is loaded.
o.deathclawCanHelp: If off, the game does not start deathclaw attacks until you turn it back on. The game turns it off by itself for a while after each attack.
o.deathclawChanceHelp: Built up each time the vault door opens and the radio attracts a dweller; added to the base chance. The game resets it to 0 after an attack. Set 0 to make attacks rarer, raise it to make them more likely.
o.deathclawCooldownHelp: Pause after an attack. Until it ends, deathclaws do not come.
o.deathclawHelp: The chance of an attack grows each time the vault door opens and each time the radio attracts a new dweller. Attacks start only in vaults with more than 60 dwellers (35 in Survival mode).
o.deathclawResetHelp: Sets the built-up chance to zero, as right after an attack.
o.eventsHelp: Visitors and attacks. How often random incidents happen is set by the game itself and is not stored in the save; here you can change the timers and chances the save keeps.
o.explorersHelp: Dwellers sent out to explore. While they are out they find caps and items and can die if their health runs out.
o.exploringTimeHelp: How long the dweller has been exploring. The longer, the stronger the enemies and the better the loot the game gives from now on.
o.freeSkipHelp: Ticked if the game lets you replace one objective for free today.
o.hintHelp: Ticked: the hint was already shown and will not appear again. Unticked: the game shows it the next time its situation happens.
o.hintsHelp: The game shows each hint once. Ticked hints count as shown and will not appear again; untick a hint to see it again.
o.incidentDoorNote: The game does not store these attackers' health in the save, so it cannot be changed. The incident can be ended.
o.incidentFinishHelp: Ends the incident as if it was dealt with: rooms go back to normal and the enemies are gone.
o.incidentNextCheckHelp: Time until the next check when the game may start a random incident. The check repeats by itself; you can postpone it.
o.incidentPauseHelp: Moves the next random incident check later, so no fire, radroaches or raiders appear until then. After it the game checks as usual.
o.incidentStartButtonHelp: The room switches to an incident; its dwellers start fighting it when you load the save.
o.incidentStartHelp: Starts in the chosen room when the save loads, as if the game started it. Attacks at the door cannot be started this way: the file does not store where the enemies stand.
o.incidentStrengthHelp: How badly the room is hit. It decides how many enemies or fires the room has.
o.incidentsHelp: Fires, radroaches, molerats, radscorpions and attacks at the door (raiders, deathclaws and others). How often incidents happen is decided by the game.
o.logNoGame: The journal phrases are read from the installed game. The game was not found, so only the values are shown.
o.lootAsRecipeHelp: The team brings the recipe of this item, not the item. Not for junk.
o.lootHelp: What the team carries from the wasteland. It all goes to storage when the team is back. Recipes take no room in the pack.
o.lootThemesHelp: Theme parts the team carries. They add to the collected parts when the team is back.
o.newObjectivesInHelp: When this time is up, the game gives new objectives and a new free replacement.
o.newQuestsInHelp: When this time is up, the game picks new daily and weekly quests.
o.noDaily: No daily or weekly quest is offered right now.
o.noExplorers: Nobody is exploring the wasteland right now.
o.noQuest: No quest has been started yet.
o.objLevelHelp: Each step raises the goal and the reward. The text above shows the goal for the chosen difficulty.
o.objectiveDone: Done, collect the reward in the game
o.quantumSkipsHelp: How many objectives were replaced for Nuka-Cola Quantum today. Each one makes the next replacement cost more; 0 gives the lowest price.
o.questMemoryHelp: The game does not offer recent and skipped quests again for a while. Remove one here and it can come up again.
o.questQuantumHelp: How many quests were skipped for Nuka-Cola Quantum. Each one makes the next skip cost more; 0 gives the lowest price.
o.questRadHelp: RadAway the quest team carries right now. It removes radiation damage during this quest.
o.questRunningNoReplace: This quest is being played now, so it cannot be replaced.
o.questStimHelp: Stimpaks the quest team carries right now. They heal dwellers during fights on this quest.
o.questTeamHealthHelp: Health and radiation of the dwellers on the quest right now.
o.questToggleHelp: Tick to mark the quest completed, untick to play it again.
o.raidersHealthHelp: Health pool of the attacking raider group.
o.ratingCollectedHelp: Ticked when the reward for this day was taken.
o.ratingHelp: Every day the game rates the vault by happiness and gives caps for it; on the seventh day it gives lunchboxes instead. A higher rating gives a bigger reward. Untick "collected" to take a day's reward again.
o.ratingNone: No days rated this week yet.
o.refugeesAllHelp: Ticked if every refugee already came. Untick so the game sends refugees again.
o.refugeesFailedHelp: Times no refugee came. Each failure raises the chance of the next try.
o.refugeesGotHelp: Refugees that already came from the current group.
o.refugeesHelp: Dwellers who come to the vault door by themselves from time to time.
o.refugeesInHelp: When this time is up, the game checks whether a refugee comes.
o.replaceObjectiveHelp: Choose another objective for this slot. Its progress starts from zero.
o.replaceQuestHelp: Choose another quest of the same kind.
o.returnInHelp: Time left on the way back.
o.returnNowHelp: The dweller arrives at the vault as soon as the game loads the save.
o.serviceHelp: Internal game data: timers, links between objects, analytics. Change it only if you know exactly what a value does; a wrong value can break the save.
o.statsHelp: Counters shown in the game's statistics window (Pip-Boy, vault statistics). They only affect what the window shows and the progress of achievements that count the same things.
o.strangerCanHelp: If off, the Stranger never appears in this vault.
o.strangerHelp: From time to time the Stranger appears in a random room for a few seconds. Tap him in the game to get caps.
o.strangerHere: He is in the vault now
o.strangerInHelp: Time until he appears. Time does not run during incidents. After each visit the game picks the next interval itself (the more rooms, the longer it is).
o.strangerLeavesHelp: How long he stays in the vault before leaving.
o.strangerNowHelp: The Stranger appears within about ten seconds after the game loads the save (not during an incident).
o.team.GoingToQuest: on the way to a quest
o.team.ResumingSurpriseQuest: going on with a surprise quest
o.team.ReturningToVault: on the way back to the vault
o.teamRadHelp: RadAway the dweller took to the wasteland. The game uses it when radiation gets high. The game allows up to 25.
o.teamStimHelp: Stimpaks the dweller took to the wasteland. The game uses them when health gets low. The game allows up to 25.
o.timerNowHelp: Sets this timer to one second: the game finishes it right after loading the save.
o.treeHelp: Any value of the file. Expert mode only.
o.treeLocked: The data tree is available in expert mode. Enable it in Settings.
o.treePick: Choose a key in the tree to view or change it.
o.tutorialMainHelp: The game teaches the basics step by step and shows hints when something happens for the first time.
o.waveFailedHelp: Ticked when the vault did not hold the previous wave off.
o.wavesHelp: Scorched raids of the ultracite season. Only season vaults have them.
page.contactsDesc: How to contact the author, including about data, rights and security.
page.desktopDesc: ShelterSave-Studio for Windows, Linux and macOS: works offline and shows game pictures from your installed game.
page.disclaimerDesc: ShelterSave-Studio is an independent project not affiliated with the rights holders of Fallout Shelter.
page.editorDesc: Free open-source editor for Fallout Shelter saves. Works in your browser: the file never leaves your device.
page.helpDesc: Where Fallout Shelter keeps its save, how to edit it and put it back, and answers to common questions.
page.licenseDesc: GPL-3.0 license, source code and third-party components.
page.noscript: The editor needs JavaScript. The help pages, legal documents and the desktop version work without it.
page.privacyDesc: What the website and the program process and what they do not.
page.storageDesc: The website sets no cookies. What it keeps in your browser and how to delete it.
page.termsDesc: Terms of using the ShelterSave-Studio website and program.
recover.done: Edits restored. Check them and save the file.
recover.text: The editor closed unexpectedly while this file had unsaved edits ({n} steps). Restore them? The file itself was not changed.
recover.title: Unsaved edits were kept
reload.discard: Load the new file without my edits
reload.done: The file was loaded again from disk.
reload.failed: {n} of your edits could not be repeated on the new file.
reload.keep: Load the new file and repeat my edits
reload.keepHelp: Your edits are made again, in the same order, on the game's newer file. Edits that no longer fit (for example, for a dweller who is gone) are skipped.
reload.text: The file on disk is newer than the one you are editing, and you have unsaved edits. Saving now would overwrite the game's progress.
reload.textClean: The file on disk is newer than the one open here. Load the new version to see the game's progress; saving the open version would overwrite it.
reload.title: The game saved this file
res.counterHelp: Kept by the game but not used to give boxes. Unopened boxes are set in the Boxes block.
review.changedOnDisk: The file on disk changed after it was opened (perhaps by the game). Saving will overwrite those changes.
review.clearSession: Delete the local copy of this session
review.closeGame: Make sure the game is closed. Otherwise it may overwrite this file.
review.downloadHint: Put the downloaded file into the game's save folder as Vault1.sav, Vault2.sav or Vault3.sav (the slot it came from), replacing the old file. The game ignores other names.
review.noChanges: There are no changes compared with the file as opened.
review.title: Review before saving
room.babyCountHelp: Usually the game rolls this at birth (twins and triplets need a pet bonus). Set it here to get twins or triplets for sure. A room needs space for every baby, otherwise the birth waits.
room.babyHelp: The game decides these when the pregnancy starts and uses them at birth: what the baby will be like.
room.babyRarityHelp: Rarer children get more SPECIAL points when they grow up.
room.babyStatHelp: The SPECIAL the child gets at its highest value; normally inherited from a parent.
room.birthHelp: Time until the baby is born.
room.brokenHelp: Ticked if raiders or deathclaws broke the vault door. Untick to repair it.
room.cloneHelp: Opens the new room form with the same type, size and level at the nearest free spot. Click the map to choose another spot. Dwellers and stored resources are not copied. Shortcut: Ctrl+D.
room.cloneNotBuildable: The game does not let you build this room.
room.cloneUnique: This room can be built only once.
room.craftNowHelp: Sets the progress to 100%. After the save is loaded the item is ready to collect in this room.
room.craftProgressHelp: Crafting progress saved in the file. The real time left depends on the dwellers working in the room.
room.craftReady: The item is ready: collect it in the room in the game.
room.damageHelp: Strength of a fire, radroaches or other incident in this room. It only matters while an incident is going on.
room.doorDamageHelp: How much the vault door is damaged by raiders or other attackers. 0 means the door is intact; when the damage reaches the door's strength, attackers break in.
room.growUpHelp: Time until the child becomes an adult dweller who can work.
room.incidentBusy: Another incident is going on in the vault; the game runs one at a time.
room.mergeCuts: Not in normal mode: through this room other rooms reach the lift, and after the change some of them would have no way to it. Expert mode allows it.
room.mergeHelp: 1–3 rooms merged. The change is only allowed if the room does not overlap neighbours.
room.mergeNeighbours: A room of the same type and level stands next to it. The game will merge them the next time you build or upgrade a room.
room.mergeNoSpace: Does not fit: neighbouring rooms or rocks are in the way on both sides.
room.powerHelp: Ticked if the room gets power. When energy runs short, the game turns rooms off and back on by itself.
room.radioInHelp: Time until the radio brings a new dweller to the vault door.
room.radioReadyHelp: Ticked when the radio has called a new dweller: tap the room in the game to let them in. Each dweller called by the radio raises the chance of a deathclaw attack a little.
room.radioVaultHelp: Ticked: the radio only makes dwellers happier. Unticked: it also calls new dwellers from the wasteland.
room.removeHelp: Dwellers of this room stay in the vault without a job, like newcomers. The change can be undone. Key: Delete.
room.storedFilling: Batch is filling: {pct}%. Not ready yet.
room.storedHelp: Output the room has made and keeps until you tap it in the game. It goes to the vault storage when collected.
room.storedReady: Batch is full: ready to collect.
room.storedRowHelp: Units ready to collect. A room fills one batch at a time; while the batch is filling the game keeps a fraction, and once it is full it rounds down and shows the collect icon. This shows whole ready units; set a full batch and the game marks the room ready as soon as dwellers work in it.
room.themeHelp: The theme is set for all rooms of this type at once. Inside the vault the game shows it only on rooms of size 3 and level 3.
room.themeHidden: This room is not size 3 and level 3, so the game shows it without the theme.
room.timersHelp: Time left for what is going on in the room. Set 0 to finish it when the game loads the save.
room.trainingHelp: Time until the dweller gains the next point of the stat this room trains.
room.withHoleHelp: Ticked if deathclaws broke through the elevator floor. Untick to close the hole.
save.exportHelp: Saves the decrypted data as readable JSON. The editor can open it again.
save.importHelp: Replaces the open data with a JSON file. You can undo this.
save.noBackups: No backups of this file yet.
save.restoreHelp: Copies a backup over the save file. The current file is backed up first.
set.backupsHelp: Before the first write to a save, a copy is made in the backup folder.
set.clearDataHelp: Deletes settings and the saved session from this browser.
set.confirmMassHelp: Ask before an action changes many records at once.
set.dwellerScrollHelp: When you open another dweller, the page either stays at the same place or goes back to the top.
set.expertText: Values outside the game norm can break the vault or make the game reset them. They are always marked with a warning. Keep a backup of your save.
set.gameDirHelp: Item pictures and dweller looks are read from your installed copy of Fallout Shelter; the editor itself ships none of them. The game folder (the one with FalloutShelter_Data) is looked for in Steam libraries; if the game is elsewhere, pick the folder by hand.
set.gameDirMismatch: The game was found, but its files differ from the version the catalog was made for: pictures are not available.
set.itemNames: Names of items, weapons and pets
set.itemNamesHelp: English names are easier to look up online. Russian names follow the official translation of the game.
set.modeHelp: Normal mode keeps values within what the game accepts. Expert mode allows any value and opens the data tree.
set.resetHelp: Returns all settings to their defaults.
set.restoreSessionHelp: Keeps the open file and its history in this browser so nothing is lost after a reload.
set.saveDirsHelp: Standard game folders are always searched. Add your own folders here.
set.statsHelp: Counts visits without cookies or identifiers. The file you edit is never sent.
set.title: Settings
start.drop: Drop the file to open it
start.foundNone: No saves found in the standard folders. Open a file manually or add a folder in Settings.
start.gameClosed: Close the game before editing its save.
start.local: The file is processed only on your device.
start.text: Choose a .sav file or drop it here. Exported JSON is accepted too.
start.title: Open a vault save
tb.gameRunningHelp: Fallout Shelter is open. While it runs it keeps its own copy of the vault and writes it over the save, so changes made here are lost. Close the game, then save the file here, then start the game.
tb.modeHelp: Normal mode keeps values within game limits and shows only clear settings. Expert mode (in Settings) opens every field of the file.
tb.reload: Reload the file from disk (for example after the game saved it)
theme.craftedHelp: The theme is crafted in the workshop and can be picked for rooms. Sets all 9 parts.
theme.help: A theme changes the look of all rooms of one type; inside the vault the game shows it only on rooms of size 3 and level 3. In the game a theme is first collected from 9 parts, then crafted in the workshop and chosen in the room upgrade window. Here you can pick a theme at once: if it is not crafted yet, it is marked crafted, as the game would do.
theme.holidaySet: A holiday theme is stored here. The game keeps it only during the holiday; at other times the rooms look standard.
theme.holidaysHelp: The game stores Christmas, Halloween and Thanksgiving in every save as "obtained, crafted, new": this is how the game works, not a broken file. They turn on by themselves during the holiday and cannot be picked at other times: the game drops them on load.
theme.noData: This save has no theme data.
theme.noPicture: No picture in the game files.
theme.pickHelp: The theme the game shows on every room of this type.
theme.title: Room themes
theme.vaultThemeHelp: Value of an old vault-wide theme window. In version 2.7 it does not change how the vault looks.
time.invalid: Enter date and time as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS
time.local: Local time of the device where the game runs
vault.addHelp: Set the quantity, then pick an item in the list: it is added to the storage at once.
vault.bonusHelp: Extra output from a successful rush. The game keeps it in each production room and moves it to the vault when you collect; the vault's own copy is not used by the game.
vault.builtLocked: built but locked: the game will crash
vault.completeCollectionHelp: Marks every weapon, outfit, pet and junk item as seen in the Survival Guide collection.
vault.fillHelp: Sets caps, food, energy, water, Stimpaks, RadAway and Nuka-Cola Quantum to 999 999.
vault.journalHelp: Entries about found items, dwellers and pets. The game marks new entries with a yellow badge until they are opened.
vault.lbHelp.0: Regular lunchbox: opens into cards with resources, caps, items or a dweller.
vault.lbHelp.1: Opens into a new Mr. Handy robot.
vault.lbHelp.3: Starter pack box with a fixed set of rewards.
vault.lockBuilt: The room is already built: locking it makes the game crash on load.
vault.lunchboxesHelp: Unopened boxes by type. The list and total in the file are updated automatically.
vault.mapHelp: Click an empty cell to build a room. Drag a room to move it, click it to change it. Rooms connect side by side; floors are linked only by elevators.
vault.markReadHelp: Clears the new badge on every unlocked journal entry and on every room theme. The entries stay.
vault.recipesHelp: Weapon, outfit and theme recipes known to the workshops. A known recipe can be crafted when there is enough junk.
vault.resourcesHelp: Amounts in the vault storage. The game limits the real capacity by its rooms.
vault.rocksHelp: Click rocks on the map to remove them, or an empty cell to place new ones.
vault.roomsHelp: Rooms of the vault. Build, move, upgrade and remove them on the map.
vault.selectRoom: Click a room on the map to change it, or an empty cell to build a new one.
vault.storageHelp: Weapons, outfits, junk and pets that are not equipped. Identical items are shown as one line.
vault.unlockRecipesHelp: Adds every weapon, outfit and theme recipe, so they can be crafted in the workshops.
vault.unlockRoomsHelp: Makes every room type available to build, without waiting for the dweller count the game normally asks for.
vault.unlocksHelp: Rooms the game unlocks by dweller count. A locked room cannot be built: the game crashes on load when such a room is already built.
warn.item_unknown: Item not in the reference data
warn.outfit_gender: Outfit that has no version for the dweller's gender: the game puts a random casual outfit on instead
warn.radiation: Radiation above maximum health or negative
warn.room_level: Room level above what this room has in the game
warn.room_merge: Room size the game does not have for this type
warn.title: Values outside the game norm
web.download.keep: Keep the session in this browser
web.download.title: File downloaded
web.loadFailed: The editor could not start in this browser. Update the browser or try another one.
web.notice.text: The save file is processed only on your device and is never sent anywhere. The site sets no cookies. Visits are counted anonymously.
web.restore.text: {file} with unsaved edits was left open on {date}. The edits are kept only in this browser.
web.restore.title: Continue the unfinished session?
web.where.androidPath: Android/data/com.bethsoft.falloutshelter/files on the phone storage. On Android 11 and newer this folder is hidden from most file managers: connect the phone to a computer or use a file manager that can open it.
web.where.back: After editing, download the result and put it back into the same folder with the same name, replacing the old file. Keep a copy of the original.
web.where.cloud: If the game syncs saves through the cloud, it may replace an edited file with the cloud copy. Turn cloud saves off before editing or check which copy the game loads.
web.where.names: The game has only three save slots, and the files are always named Vault1.sav, Vault2.sav and Vault3.sav. The game ignores files with any other name.
web.where.steamPath: Press Win+R, paste %LOCALAPPDATA%\FalloutShelter and press Enter.
web.where.title: Where is the save file?
